cards.text: Friend, this one's heavy, so we're going to take it slow together. After some time, David's son Amnon falls in love with Tamar, the beautiful sister of David's son Absalom. Amnon is so frustrated over her that he's sick with it.

cards.question: But Amnon can't see how he could ever do anything to Tamar. Why not?

answers.text: She was promised to a prince

cards.text: Now meet Jonadab, Amnon's friend and cousin, the son of David's brother Shimeah. The Bible calls him a very shrewd man.

cards.question: Jonadab notices something is off with Amnon. He asks why the son of the king looks so ___ morning after morning.
When Jonadab asks what's wrong, Amnon tells him he's in love with Tamar, his brother Absalom's sister.

cards.text: Jonadab, the shrewd one, has a plan. Amnon should lie down on his bed and pretend he's ill.

cards.question: When David comes to see Amnon, what does Jonadab say Amnon should ask for?

answers.text: Tamar to come make him food

cards.text: So Amnon lies down and fakes being sick. When the king comes to see him, Amnon asks for Tamar to come make a couple of cakes in front of him, so he can eat from her hand.

cards.question: David sends word to Tamar at the palace to go to her brother Amnon's house and prepare a meal for him.

cards.text: So Tamar goes to Amnon's house, where he's lying down. She kneads the dough, makes the cakes right in front of him and bakes them.

cards.question: Tamar sets the pan down in front of Amnon, and he eats right away.
Amnon refuses to eat what Tamar made. Instead, what does he order?

cards.text: Everyone goes out. Now Amnon has one more request for Tamar.

cards.question: Amnon tells Tamar to bring the food into the ___ so he can eat it from her hand.

cards.text: Tamar takes the cakes she made and goes into her brother Amnon's bedroom. Stay close, friend.
Tamar brings the cakes to Amnon. He takes hold of her and tells her to lie with him.

cards.question: Tamar cries out, "No, my brother!" She says such a thing should never be done in ___.
Tamar asks Amnon where she could ever take her shame. Then she warns him what he would be like if he does this. What?

answers.text: One of the fools in Israel
A king who loses his crown

cards.question: Tamar pleads with Amnon to speak to the king, telling him the king will not withhold her from him.

cards.text: But Amnon refuses to listen to her. Being stronger, he violates her.

cards.question: After what he did, what does Amnon feel toward Tamar?

answers.text: Hatred greater than his love before
Sorrow over what he has done
Fear of what the king will do

cards.question: Amnon tells Tamar, "Get up!" and "Be gone!" Tamar quietly agrees to go.
Tamar tells Amnon that sending her away is ___ than the great wrong he has already done to her.

cards.text: But again, Amnon refuses to listen to her. Instead, he calls for his attendant.

cards.question: What does Amnon tell his attendant to do with Tamar?

answers.text: Throw her out and bolt the door
Take her back to the palace

cards.text: The attendant throws her out and bolts the door behind her. Tamar is wearing a robe of many colors, the kind the king's virgin daughters wore.

cards.question: Outside that bolted door, how does Tamar show her grief?

answers.text: Puts ashes on her head and tears her robe
Covers her face and sits down by the gate
Pulls her robe tight and runs to the palace

cards.text: With her hand on her head, she goes away crying aloud. Her brother Absalom asks her, "Has your brother Amnon been with you?"

cards.question: Absalom tells Tamar to go straight to the king.
Absalom tells Tamar to be quiet for now and not take it to heart. So Tamar lives in Absalom's house as a ___ woman.
When King David hears all this, he is furious.
Absalom never says a word to Amnon, either good or bad. Why?

answers.text: He hated Amnon for violating Tamar
David told him to stay silent

cards.text: We're pausing right here, friend. Absalom won't give Amnon one word, good or bad. Believe me, this family's story keeps going.

findings.problem: The question asks why it seemed implausible for Amnon to do anything to Tamar and makes 'She was a virgin' the reason. In 2 Samuel 13:2, 'for she was a virgin' explains why Amnon was sick with frustration. The text does not give a reason for the implausibility, so the card adds a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'joyful' and 'honored' don't fit right after Tamar is assaulted, thrown out and crying aloud. No thoughtful baker would pick 'joyful' in particular, so it reads as a throwaway answer and doesn't match the tone of the right answer.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'He never learned what happened' is already ruled out by earlier cards. In card 14, Absalom asks Tamar 'Has your brother Amnon been with you?', and card 16 says she lives in his house. Those setup cards eliminate this answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The middle sentence, 'Absalom won't give Amnon one word, good or bad,' repeats what card 18 just covered (2 Samuel 13:22). It doesn't move the passage forward. Since the last verse was already asked on a choice card, this card can be just the line saying the story continues.

Its only guidance on tone is that his personality 'fits whatever moment he's in.' For example: no humor at all, how much of Papa Dorin's voice to keep on story cards, preferred wording for the act (such as the BSB's 'violated'), and whether to open with a gentle note like the 'this one's heavy' line used here.
